I've been farming this land for 8 years and I know Quzhou's conditions well — hot summers, cold winters, limited rainfall, and my well pump to make up the difference. My 4.1 mu isn't much, but between the wheat-maize rotation and some cotton, I keep the household fed and earn some cash. A few family members work in town, so I can't always count on their labor during peak times, which shapes how I plan things.

**My thinking:**

For the wheat-maize rotation, I'll put about 2.6 mu into it. Wheat goes in October, I harvest it in June, then I plant maize directly into the stubble — no-till saves me time and diesel. Wheat I'll use Jimai varieties, the kind my neighbors use and that the ag station recommends. For maize I'll buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed like I always do — the yield is reliable.

Cotton gets the remaining 1.5 mu. I'll plough it in spring before planting. I use the hybrid Bt cotton seed; it cuts down on bollworm spraying a lot. Cotton brings in more cash per mu than grain but it also takes more labor, especially at harvest. With some family members off-farm, I keep the cotton plot small enough that my wife and I can manage it, maybe with my parents helping during picking.

For fertilizer I follow roughly what the village tech person suggests — base fertilizer before sowing, then urea as topdressing. I use the well 3 times for wheat, twice for maize, and 4 times for cotton since it's thirstier during flowering and boll setting.
